# Brownian Motion
## What is a Brownian Motion
:::{#def-brownianMotion}
## Brownian Motion

$(B_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is a stochastic process defined on $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, P)$, i.e. for $\forall t\geq 0$, $B_t$ is a RV. $(B_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is called BM if $B_0=0$ and $\forall 0=t_0<t_1\cdots<t_i$, 
$B_{t_1}-B_{t_0}, B_{t_2}-B_{t_1}, \cdots, B_{t_i} - B_{t_{i-1}}$ are all independent and $\forall s<t, B_t-B_s \overset{(d)}{=}N(0, t-s)$.
:::

:::{#def-brownianMotion2}
## Definition Using Filtration

$(B_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is called BM w.r.t filtration $(\mathcal{F}_t)$ if 

* $B_t$ is continuous path, $B_0=0$
* $\forall t$, $B_t$ is measurable w.r.t $\mathcal{F}_t$ or $\mathcal{F}_t^{B_y}\subset\mathcal{F}_t$, where $\mathcal{F}_t^{B_t}$ is the $\sigma$ algebra generate by $B_t$
* $B_t-B_s\perp F_s$ and $B_t-B_s\overset{(d)}{=}N(0, t-s)$
:::

:::{.callout-tip}
## Properties

1. $(B_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is a martingle w.r.t to $(\mathcal{F}_t)_{t\geq 0}$.
    $$
    \begin{align}
    E(B_t|\mathcal{F}_s) &= E(B_s + B_t - B_s|\mathcal{F}_s) = B_s + E(B_t-B_s|\mathcal{F}_s) \\
    &=B_s + E(B_t-B_s) = B_s
    \end{align}
    $$

2. $B_t^2 - t$ is a martingle w.r.t. $\mathcal{F}_{t\geq 0}$.
    
    $$
    \begin{align}
    E(B^2_t-t|\mathcal{F}_s) &= E((B_s + (B_t-B_s))^2 - t | \mathcal{F}_s)\\
    &=E(B^2_s + 2B_s(B_t-B_s) + (B_t-B_s)^2|\mathcal{F}_s) - t\\
    &=B_s^2 + 2B_sE(B_t-B_s|\mathcal{F}_s) + E((B_t-B_s)^2|\mathcal{F}_s) - t\\
    &=B^2_s-s
    \end{align}
    $$
